explain.say: See the clear curved front? That is the cornea, your eye's window. As light passes through it, it bends a lot, which is called refraction. The cornea does most of the focusing. Where does light enter first?

explain.say: The iris! Now the clever bit. The ciliary muscles squeeze or relax to change the lens shape. Fat lens for near things, like a book; thin lens for far things, like a mountain. This changing is called accommodation. Which shape for reading?

faq.a: The cornea is the clear front of the eye. It bends incoming light the most and starts focusing it.

faq.q: Why does the pupil change size?
faq.a: The iris muscles make the pupil smaller in bright light to protect the retina, and wider in dim light to let more light in.
asks: Why do pupils get bigger in the dark?

faq.q: How does the lens focus on near and far things?
faq.a: The ciliary muscles change the lens shape. A fatter lens focuses near objects; a thinner lens focuses distant ones.
asks: What is accommodation of the eye?

faq.a: The retina is a layer of light-sensitive cells at the back of the eye. It turns the image into electrical signals.

faq.q: Why is the image on the retina upside down?
faq.a: A converging lens system makes a real, inverted image. The brain learns to interpret it the right way up.

facts: The cornea does about two thirds of the eye's focusing.
The image formed on the retina is real and inverted; the brain interprets it upright.

wrong.0: The retina detects light; it does not change shape to focus.
wrong.1: The optic nerve carries signals to the brain.

quiz.why: The iris narrows the pupil to protect the retina from too much light.

wrong.1: It gets bigger in dim light, to let more light in.
wrong.2: The pupil only shrinks; it never closes completely.
